description: B.Tech CSE student passionate about AI/ML, Python, Data Science, and Web Development. Participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 with Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data. Our team aims to build an AI-powered solution using NASA data to support smarter farming.
summary: Crop Compass is a farmer-friendly web app for the Field Shift challenge. Farmers face seven pressures at once: shifting temperature, changing rainfall, water shortages, extreme weather, declining soil health, crop diseases and local market conflict. The information they need is scattered, so they cannot compare options before committing land and money. A farmer enters their location, soil, current crop, water access and up to three priorities. Crop Compass pulls live NASA POWER weather for that exact point, shows NASA GIBS/MODIS satellite imagery on a map, and compares three crop rotations (Baseline, Water-smart, Soil-regeneration). It explains trade-offs, risks and missing information instead of giving a single score, using transparent rules that can be explained to a farmer. It works in four languages, with a simple farmer mode, an expert mode and voice read-aloud, and runs in any phone browser.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Crop Compass answers one question: "What should we grow next to protect our land for the future?" The farmer enters location, soil, current crop, water access and up to three priorities (for example Save Water or Improve Soil Health). The app then:

- Fetches live NASA POWER data (temperature, rainfall, humidity, sun) for that exact location, with a live-data badge.

- Shows NASA GIBS / MODIS satellite imagery on an interactive map.

- Compares three rotations: Baseline (Rice > Wheat > Fallow), Water-smart (Millet > Chickpea > Moong) and Soil-regeneration (Maize+Cowpea > Chickpea > Sunn hemp).

- Scores each rotation on water, soil, climate resilience, input cost and economic stability, weighted by the farmer's priorities, and shows the trade-offs on a radar chart.

- Lists risks (disease, market dependence) and "missing information" (such as soil tests) for each rotation, so it supports local experts rather than replacing them.

- Labels every figure as live, historical, farmer-provided or model estimate.

- Offers Farmer Friendly and Expert Science modes, four languages (English, Hindi, Punjabi, Spanish) and voice read-aloud.

HOW WE BUILT IT

Stack: React, Tailwind CSS and Leaflet, deployed as a static site on Vercel. The design is modular, so new NASA datasets plug into the same rotation engine. We chose transparent rule-based scoring over a black-box model so every recommendation can be explained to and trusted by a farmer.

ILLUSTRATIVE RESULTS (Punjab rice-wheat demo farm)

The water-smart rotation cuts water use by about 52% (about 1,700 mm to about 820 mm), and legume-based rotations fix about 140-260 kg of nitrogen per hectare. These are model estimates from crop-water and legume literature, not NASA measurements. Actual results vary by soil, season and variety.

COVERAGE OF THE SEVEN PRESSURES

Built: water shortages, declining soil health. Partial: shifting temperature, changing rainfall, extreme weather, crop diseases, local market conflict (risks are flagged now; frost, pest-risk scoring and live prices are next).

HONEST LIMITS

Today the rotation scores come from the farm profile and agronomy rules; NASA data powers the live farm view (weather and imagery). Feeding NASA trends into the scoring is our next step. If the internet is unavailable, the app falls back to illustrative baseline data and says so. Satellite resolution is coarse, results are estimates, and crop rules need validation against FAO/ICAR guidance and local tests.

FEASIBILITY AND ROADMAP

The working prototype has 5 preset farms across India, the USA and Kenya. NASA POWER is free and needs no API key, and static hosting keeps running cost near zero. Natural partners are extension officers, agri-NGOs and researchers.

Now: prototype, live POWER data, 3 rotations.

Next: what-if sliders, confidence labels, SMAP soil moisture and GPM rainfall.

Later: SRTM slope, GRACE-FO groundwater, field pilots, offline use.

TEAM

Team Dark Neutrino, G.C.R.G Group of Institutions: Zaid, Vishal Jaiswal, Mohammad Asif, Arsh Shukla, Aman Ali.
